changes.before: Flexible orchestration is the default recommended option for new deployments in this lesson; choose Uniform when the workload requires identical instances.
changes.after: Flexible orchestration is recommended for new deployments and supports identical or mixed VMs. Choose Uniform when its scale-set VM model and feature set fit the workload.
changes.reason: Identical instances alone do not require Uniform; Flexible also supports identical VMs.

changes.before: Configure autoscale profiles with minimum, maximum and safe default instance counts. The default is used when metrics are unavailable.
changes.after: Configure autoscale profiles with minimum, maximum and safe default instance counts. When metrics are unavailable, autoscale scales out to the default only if current capacity is lower; it does not scale in to the default.
changes.reason: Default capacity is a scale-out fallback, not an unconditional reset.

changes.before: A rule combines a metric or schedule trigger with a scale-in or scale-out action.
changes.after: A metric rule combines a trigger with a scale-in or scale-out action. Scheduled profiles apply capacity limits and rules at specified times.
changes.reason: Distinguish metric-rule triggers from schedules on autoscale profiles.

changes.before: Automatic scaling is a separate HTTP-traffic-driven feature on supported Premium tiers, using always-ready instances without custom rules.
changes.after: Automatic scaling is a separate HTTP-traffic-driven feature on Premium v2, v3 and v4, configured per app with always-ready instances and no custom scaling rules.
changes.reason: Current docs include Premium v4 and per-app scaling.

changes.before: Do not assume a backup captures every external dependency. Confirm database protection and supported restore behavior for the chosen configuration.
changes.after: Automatic backups exclude linked databases. Custom backups support only specified linked database types; protect other dependencies separately and verify restore support.
changes.reason: Replace a generic caution with the concrete automatic/custom database distinction.

changes.before: Containers generally use fewer resources and start faster, but their isolation is not equivalent to a full VM security boundary.
changes.after: Containers generally use fewer resources and start faster. Typical process-isolated containers share the host kernel and provide a weaker security boundary than a full VM.
changes.reason: Qualify the generic comparison so it does not imply all container isolation models have the same boundary.

changes.before: Choose the CPU and memory allocation when deploying the container group; its resource allocation is fixed for its lifetime.
changes.after: Choose CPU and memory when deploying the container group. Changing its CPU, memory or GPU allocation requires deleting and recreating the group.
changes.reason: Explain what fixed allocation means operationally.

changes.before: Container Instances supports Windows and Linux containers and Azure Files mounts for persistent storage.
changes.after: Container Instances supports Windows and Linux containers. Azure Files volume mounts for persistent storage are supported only for Linux containers.
changes.reason: Windows container groups do not support Azure Files mounts.

changes.before: A container group schedules containers on the same host; they share lifecycle, local networking, storage volumes and group resources.
changes.after: A container group schedules containers on the same host; they share lifecycle, local networking, storage volumes and group resources. Multi-container groups support Linux only; Windows groups support one container.
changes.reason: Add the platform limitation missing from the training unit.

changes.before: Azure VM backup uses workload extensions and disk snapshots. Vaults hold recovery points and backup policies.
changes.after: Azure VM backup takes disk snapshots. Application- or filesystem-consistent backups use a VM extension; supported agentless backups are crash-consistent. Vaults manage recovery points and policies.
changes.reason: Current VM backup supports agentless crash-consistent backups; extensions are not universal.

changes.before: Cross-subscription restore requires the vault property to be enabled and a supported managed VM within the same tenant. Snapshot-tier recovery points are not supported.
changes.after: Cross-subscription restore uses vault-tier points for supported managed VMs in the same tenant. Restore to a subscription other than the protected VM or vault subscription requires the vault setting; ADE- and customer-key-encrypted disks are unsupported.
changes.reason: Current docs distinguish protected/vault subscriptions and exclude encrypted disk configurations.

changes.before: Azure automatically collects VM host metrics and activity logs. Guest data needs Azure Monitor Agent and data collection rules.
changes.after: Azure automatically collects VM host metrics and activity logs. Configure Azure Monitor Agent and data collection rules for guest performance counters and event logs.
changes.reason: Scope the agent requirement to the guest telemetry demonstrated rather than every application telemetry method.

changes.before: VM insights helps install the agent, configure common performance collection and show curated performance workbooks.
changes.after: The lesson uses classic logs-based VM insights: Azure Monitor Agent collects common guest performance data into Log Analytics for curated charts and workbooks. Current monitoring also offers OpenTelemetry metrics stored in an Azure Monitor workspace.
changes.reason: Label the classic lesson workflow because current portal onboarding defaults to OpenTelemetry metrics.

changes.before: Enable VM insights from the VM Insights page and configure its data collection rule and Log Analytics workspace.
changes.after: The lesson demonstrates classic logs-based VM insights with a data collection rule and Log Analytics workspace. Current portal onboarding uses Monitor and Configure, with OpenTelemetry metrics selected by default and a logs-based option.
changes.reason: Current portal no longer matches the universal Insights/Enable instruction in the old unit.

changes.before: VM insights installs Azure Monitor Agent and collects a predefined set of guest performance counters. Allow time for installation and data ingestion.
changes.after: For classic logs-based monitoring, Azure Monitor Agent collects a predefined set of guest performance counters. Allow time for agent installation and data ingestion.
changes.reason: Scope the statement to the demonstrated classic workflow.

changes.before: View the collected counters in Insights performance workbooks; this rule sends data to Azure Monitor Logs rather than Metrics Explorer.
changes.after: View classic logs-based counters in VM insights performance charts and workbooks. These counters go to Log Analytics; OpenTelemetry monitoring instead stores metrics in an Azure Monitor workspace.
changes.reason: Avoid presenting classic Logs storage as the only current guest monitoring model.

changes.before: Optional process and dependency mapping adds a view of connected application components.
changes.after: VM insights Map and Dependency Agent are deprecated and retire on 30 June 2028. New portal onboarding ended on 30 September 2025; do not enable them for new deployments.
changes.reason: The training unit still suggests enabling an optional Map feature that current product docs explicitly deprecate.

changes.before: Set the destination to a Log Analytics workspace; configure the collection endpoint as required by the demonstrated setup.
changes.after: Send Syslog to a Log Analytics workspace. The lesson creates a data collection endpoint, but ordinary public-endpoint Syslog collection does not require one; Private Link does.
changes.reason: Correct the implication that the illustrated endpoint is always required.
